metadata.description: The portable OS-patching process — the definition BOTH engines share (blue today, green tomorrow). Names no engine: this is what org policy gates, what schedules reference, what compliance reports against, and what any provider must satisfy to declare `execute_workflows / Automation.OSPatch`.

inputs_schema.description: The typed parameters the run accepts (a declarative JSON-Schema for the run's inputs).

outputs_schema.description: The typed results the run publishes (E2 — every engine must satisfy it).

idempotency.description: Re-run semantics — a bounded codelist (PVD-001 form b), fixed semantics not a growing vocabulary.

compensation.description: What undo means, if anything — a bounded codelist. Rollback is a DIFFERENT process type, declared honestly.

affected_entities.description: Which records this run may mutate — the blast-radius declaration (references).

targets.description: The hosts to patch — references to Compute.* hosts or a DCMGroup (refines the Base inputs).

patch_policy.description: What to patch — a bounded codelist (PVD-001).

reboot_policy.description: Reboot behaviour — a bounded codelist; `if-required` may reference a maintenance window.

exclusions.description: The org's known-fragile packages to hold back.

last_run_status.description: Outcome of the most recent patch run (succeeded | failed | partial) — the readiness signal schedules and compliance reports consume.

last_run_timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant of the most recent run completion.

packages_updated.description: Count of packages changed in the most recent run — the drift-facing magnitude signal.

context.purpose: The portable OS-patching process — what org policy gates, schedules reference, and compliance reports against, independent of which engine executes it.
context.plain_description: Declares that hosts get patched: which package sets, within which maintenance windows, at which severity floor. Both engines (blue today, green tomorrow) satisfy this one definition — swapping engines never touches the declared process.
use_when: You schedule or gate OS patching as governed automation
You need engine-portable patch compliance reporting
